source.title: Automatic Document Selection for Efficient Encoder Pretraining
source.authors: Yukun Feng; Patrick Xia; Benjamin Van Durme; João Sedoc

record.tranche_reason: The study varies the amount and selection strategy of pretraining data and reports held-out pretraining perplexity, but it does not fit or evaluate a power law.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 and its accompanying text report held-out Pile perplexity across training-data amounts: perplexity decreases as the amount of training data increases for both cynical and random selection. The study does not test parameter-count or compute scaling, or whether this trend has a power-law form. It reports no results testing V2–V7.
record.test_reason: This is a data-selection study. It cites Kaplan et al. but fits no scaling law. Its only data-amount sweep covers 1%, 2% and 5% of the Pile, about a 5x range, at a fixed 100k steps, so training steps may be the bottleneck. Its results cannot show a power-law form, exponents, extrapolation or allocation. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that document-level cynical selection from the Pile gives lower target-domain perplexity than random selection. It also gives comparable or better Edge Probing results with 20x less data, 3x fewer iterations and about 2x lower compute cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates document selection for encoder pretraining, not the original scaling-law measurement or fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Data-selection strategy and training-data amount; the study reports that cynical selection has higher held-out Pile perplexity than random selection, despite better adaptation to the target domain.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 100k steps, held-out Pile perplexity falls as random or cynical training data grows from 1% to 5%. Cynical selection gives higher general-corpus perplexity but lower target-domain perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The data-selection strategy shifts how pretraining loss on general vs target-domain data depends on dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: Target-domain (OntoNotes) perplexity at 100k steps is lowest at 2% cynical data, and more data does not help (Fig. 2 right). The 1% run leads in training loss until the 2% run overtakes it later (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a fixed step budget, smaller targeted datasets can match or beat larger ones on in-domain loss.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study uses one source corpus and one target domain, does not run multiple random-selection seeds, and reports held-out Pile perplexity values only in a figure rather than giving the values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported held-out pretraining perplexity results left out.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents, range of several orders of magnitude, parameter and compute scaling.
All. The Edge Probing scores vs data amount (Fig. 3) are three to four points with no predictability analysis.

missing.what: OntoNotes (target-domain) validation perplexity vs data amount for cynical and random selection at 100k steps. This is non-monotone for cynical selection, lowest at 2%.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and its V1 limits_scope label are not supported. The sweep is too narrow and has no fit, and the paper's aim is data selection, not scaling. Mentions of Kaplan et al. are citations only.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law form and exponents; several-orders-of-magnitude range; parameter-count and compute scaling; conditions where other factors are not the bottleneck.
